extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulemaking participants and technical stakeholders (industry, environmental advocates, consultants, and regulatory modelers) involved in CCR risk assessment and notice-and-comment reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and policy standards EPA uses to evaluate modeling, data, and interpretation in the 2024 Coal Combustion Residuals (CCR) Risk Assessment and related rulemaking responses to public comments. Focuses on model selection, documentation, exposure pathways, data sources, and policy interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate interpretation of aggregated summary graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphs that summarize modeled results must not inappropriately aggregate across dissimilar cohorts (e.g., age cohorts) or otherwise bias plotted risks low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA determined the referenced graph "incorrectly summarized model results for receptors of all age cohorts into one figure," which can bias results low. Aggregations must preserve relevant subgroup distinctions and sample size must be sufficient to reflect national variability before drawing broader conclusions. If filtered subsets yield relatively few model runs, do not rely on that line of evidence for national rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inferring a safe unit-size threshold from limited modeling summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not appropriate to use a single graph or summary to identify a specific unit size below which landfill risks are not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The graph summarized 2014 model results (modeling receptors up to a mile away) and cannot be used to identify a unit-size 'safe' threshold; EPA cautions against extrapolating landfill graphs to different unit types (e.g., surface impoundments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater protection as independent regulatory concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Groundwater contamination is a significant concern that merits regulatory action in its own right, whether or not the aquifer is currently used as a source of drinking water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory decisions should protect groundwater resources irrespective of current use; contamination potential alone justifies regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection must support unsaturated and saturated zone simulation and sequential flow/transport
rubrics_metrics.description: Model software should be capable of simulating flow and transport in both the unsaturated and saturated zones without the need for additional modeling packages and simulate groundwater flow and transport sequentially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA selected MODFLOW—Unstructured Grid (USG) for its ability to: (1) simulate flow/transport in both zones without additional packages; and (2) simulate flow and transport sequentially without cell-by-cell reading. Choice of code should be justified by these capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use transient (time-series) simulations for plume evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Steady-state simulations should not be used when representation of plume evolution over time is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Steady state simulations were not used because they do not provide a time series representation of plume evolution." Use transient simulations to capture how plumes develop and change over decades/centuries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient model documentation without requiring impractically large raw outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide enough model documentation (inputs, assumptions, summary outputs) to evaluate model design and results, while recognizing impracticality of distributing prohibitively large raw output files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviewed model documentation and noted it did not include full output files for all MODFLOW runs because file size would be prohibitively large. Level of documentation should be consistent across model components (e.g., EPACMTP) and correct typographical input discrepancies when identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not base final regulatory decisions on draft toxicity values
rubrics_metrics.description: Use finalized toxicity values (e.g., IRIS values) as the best available data; do not base final actions on draft reassessments that are subject to revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA used the current IRIS cancer slope factor for arsenic (1.5 mg/kg/d−1). Although a draft reassessment could change estimates substantially, it is not finalized and therefore cannot form the basis for a final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additivity of carcinogenic risks across chemical and radiological contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy is to treat the risk resulting from exposure to multiple carcinogens as additive and to evaluate radionuclide risks in the same manner as chemical contaminants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA policy treats chemical and radiological carcinogenic risks additively; separating them would not change overall conclusions in this assessment since each class can individually exceed levels of concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent leachable content using LEAF data, not COALQUAL
rubrics_metrics.description: For modeling groundwater exposure, do not use COALQUAL to estimate leachable content; represent leachable content using available LEAF data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous reviews did not identify bulk content as a sensitive parameter for leachable content; even at lower bulk concentrations, sufficient soluble mass may support sustained leaching. Use leaching-specific datasets (LEAF) for fate/transport modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use COALQUAL cautiously for bulk activity estimates and cross-validate
rubrics_metrics.description: COALQUAL can provide a reasonable estimate of median and high-end ash activity for bulk radionuclide content (thorium/uranium), but cross-validate and adjust weighting for region/coal rank as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA reviewed COALQUAL and literature, removed duplicative/nonrepresentative samples, updated weighting with EIA production data, and concluded COALQUAL aligns reasonably with updated datasets. Expect some differences between datasets developed by different methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and correct dataset/sample characterization errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and correct duplicative samples, misdescribed samples, and unintended averaging that bias datasets toward facilities with many samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA removed duplicative samples and one unrepresentative study; updated the database and summary statistics. Dataset curation steps should be documented and corrections summarized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterministic sensitivity approach for radon when national-scale probabilistic parameters unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: When national-scale default parameters for radon are not available, use a deterministic analysis specifying high/moderate/low input values to capture potential exposure ranges and identify central tendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA modeled baseline with moderate values, then adjusted inputs up/down to see which inputs most influence risk and to develop an RME scenario. If emanation from CCR is indistinguishable from background, do not retain quantitative radon evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate bounding scenarios including uncovered CCR to inform sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Include scenarios without soil cover (uncovered CCR) as bounding estimates when there is potential for lack of cover or initial construction that covers CCR may not be maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluated a scenario of CCR without any soil cover to provide a bounding estimate and link primary and sensitivity analyses; recognize it is unlikely future residential construction would occur without some initial soil cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of PRG calculator to CCR intermixed with soil
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRG calculator is applicable to scenarios of CCR intermixed with soil because exposure assumptions (incidental ingestion and direct gamma exposure) are relevant for small particulates intermingled with soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA disagrees that PRG calculator is inappropriate; model parameters for gamma exposure are generally the same as RESRAD, and many inputs reflect Agency policy for RME scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: National risk assessments focus on waste contributions; background handled site-specifically
rubrics_metrics.description: In national risk assessments under RCRA, EPA generally considers contributions from disposed wastes to risk; consideration of background concentrations is more appropriate at site-specific risk management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background may sometimes be higher than modeled concentrations, but national-scale incorporation of background is unlikely to change conclusions and is better handled during site-specific corrective action evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-identified GWPS exceedances do not require a statistical-significance test
rubrics_metrics.description: A statistically significant increase above a Groundwater Protection Standard (GWPS) is not an appropriate requirement for identifying modeled exceedances in numerical fate/transport models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical testing is used in monitoring programs because of sampling variability; numerical models track contaminant mass from release to exposure and do not require additional statistical confirmation that an identified exceedance resulted from leakage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical standards for incorporating site-specific monitoring data into national models
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not incorporate unvetted site-specific monitoring data into national probabilistic modeling because of data quality, representativeness, incompleteness of posting, and impracticality of thorough compilation for many units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring networks often have deficiencies (wells too far apart, wrong aquifer, poorly installed). Using these data would require thorough review; probabilistic characterization using local data sources is preferred to capture national variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limitations of groundwater monitoring snapshots
rubrics_metrics.description: Groundwater monitoring samples provide snapshots in time and do not convey source leachate magnitude, leakage duration, or long-term plume progression needed for fate/transport modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring requires repeated sampling and statistical analysis to determine exceedances relative to background; incorporation into models would require additional assumptions and could increase uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret sensitivity analyses in context of modeled unit types and parameter ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sensitivity analyses are interpreted with awareness of the underlying model run populations (e.g., inclusion of lined units can mask effects) and check that parameter ranges include extreme conditions if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA noted that a 2014 pH sensitivity analysis included many lined units which can mask pH effects; few runs existed for highly acidic pH. Sensitivity analysis must have adequate representation across relevant parameter space to support conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider extreme pH and co-disposal impacts on leaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Modeling should account for the potential for extreme pH (highly acidic or highly basic) and co-disposal with coal refuse to affect leaching behavior and increase risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available LEAF data show some constituents leach at highest concentrations near pH extremes; EPA observed higher risks at pH ~13 and noted porewater data showing pH near 1 in some samples. Co-disposal has been associated with impacts to porewater and groundwater in observed cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for current prevalence and performance of liners, including corrective action rates
rubrics_metrics.description: National risk estimates should account for updated information on the prevalence of unlined units and evidence that some liner systems do not achieve performance standards (e.g., units in corrective action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA found a greater proportion of regulated units have no engineered liner and about 10% of regulated units with composite/alternate liners entered corrective action, indicating potential for higher national risks than previously modeled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize exposure pathways with greatest contribution to risk
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple pathways exist, prioritize pathways that drive risk (e.g., incidental ingestion and direct gamma exposure) and consider others (e.g., inhalation) only if they materially increase calculated risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA found PRG defaults for inhalation of uranium-238 chain are orders of magnitude higher than for gamma exposure or ingestion, making inhalation unlikely to substantially increase calculated risk at the national scale; pathway-specific modeling inputs (vegetative cover, wind) add uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct discrepancies in model inputs across coupled tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and correct typographical or input discrepancies between linked modeling tools (e.g., EPACMTP and MODFLOW) to ensure consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA identified a typo discrepancy between EPACMTP and MODFLOW inputs which was corrected; such errors should be fixed and documented in updated assessment materials.
